A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same path-variance-based density ratio estimation work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B support comparison despite the changed title and method name.

before.justification: v1 reports original mutual-information and density-estimation experiments, component ablations, and learned-path analyses in Section 5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results, including numerical comparisons in Tables 1–4 and 6 and density-estimation visualizations.

M1.justification: MinPV is renamed MVP. The KMM parameterization, affine and spherical constraints, DI/DDBI objectives, adaptive weighting, timestep sampling, and inference procedures remain unchanged, including Algorithms 1–3.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same five pathological MI tasks, high-dimensional Gaussian settings, six structured 2D datasets, and five tabular datasets. Sections 5 and B.4–B.6 introduce no new task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain Linear, VP, Cosine, Föllmer, and Trigonometric paths in the corresponding experiments. The changed VP citation does not change the evaluated baseline or its formulation.

E3.justification: The DI/DDBI task assignments, dimensions, correlation settings, KMM component counts, path constraints, metrics, and stated preprocessing and splits are retained. No evaluation procedure or experimental setting is revised.

E4.justification: The KMM-component and path-constraint ablations, pathological-distribution robustness tests, and optimized-path analyses are unchanged. Appendix B retains the same supplementary evidence; relabeled plots do not constitute new analyses.

E5.justification: Table 3 retains mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting, and Tables 1 and 4 retain their existing uncertainty entries. Neither version adds or revises repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Result entries and plotted curves are unchanged. For example, Table 3 retains the affine d=160 estimate of 40.59 ± 0.55 and MSE 1.02; Table 4 retains spherical BSDS300 NLL of -143.97 ± 0.22. The appendix results also match.

T1.justification: Lemma 4.1, Theorem 4.2, Proposition 4.3, and the assumptions and proofs in Appendix A remain mathematically unchanged. Renaming the principle and replacing some I notation with MI in B.4 do not alter definitions or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract broadens its framing from DRE-specific time scores to score-based methods generally, adds a present-tense claim of a general framework for score-based interpolation, and omits the earlier explicit heuristic qualifier. Broader applicability was previously discussed as future work; the central DRE contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Sections 4.1 and 5.5 and Remark A.3 retain the same substantive qualifications: variance minimization is a heuristic, a tighter error bound is not guaranteed, and control of the Lipschitz constant is empirical. Result interpretations and future-work limitations are also retained.

D1.justification: v4 adds a direct code-repository hyperlink in the abstract, whereas v1 only promises a future release. Implementation details remain unchanged, and v4 still retains that future-release statement. The PDFs establish a new access pointer, not the repository's contents or functionality.

R1.justification: Sections 5.1 and B.1 replace the VP-path citation to Jiaming Song et al.'s Denoising Diffusion Implicit Models with Yang Song et al.'s already-cited SDE paper. The DDIM reference is removed; the substantive related-work discussion otherwise remains stable.

P1.justification: The title is shortened, MinPV becomes MVP, and the abstract and opening motivation are rewritten. Some MI notation and headings are adjusted, but the section sequence, appendix organization, and most explanatory prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table labels, captions, and plot legends are updated for MVP, including the KMM prior/posterior labels in appendix plots. Limited text and equation reflow occurs, while figure membership, table organization, axes, density images, and plotted curves are preserved.

improvement.justification: The concrete code pointer and corrected VP-path attribution modestly improve access information and traceability. Scientific evidence is unchanged, and the broader abstract receives no additional validation, although the body retains its heuristic qualifications. The stale future-release statement limits the clarity of the access update; the overall gain is small.
